the study of the molecular mechanisms that underlie translation regulation and its role in the pathogenesis of cancer.

the study of the specific features of protein biosynthetic apparatus and the molecular mechanisms of its functioning, including the mechanisms of translation elongation and the control of translation by tRNAs, ARSs, elongation factor eIF1A and microRNA.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the translation elongation machinery in higher eukaries is much more sophisticated than it was previously thought.
the higher eukaryotics translation machinery is much more complex than that in bacteria, and the mechanisms of its regulation are much more complicated.
the translation machinery is a highly dynamic and flexible system that can adapt its functions to different cellular needs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the eEF1H complex is the most important component of the protein synthesis machinery in higher eukaries and that eEF1A is the most important protein in the complex.

the eukaryotic ribosome is a complex molecular machine with a high degree of functional compartmentalization that is able to control the rate of translation and the fidelity of the translation process.
the eEF1H complex is a key regulator of protein synthesis in higher eukaries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
eukaryotic protein biosynthesis is an extremely complicated and highly regulated process that is controlled by the coordinated activity of many different proteins and RNA molecules.
the mechanisms of translation elongation in mammalian cells are more complex than in prokaryotic cells.
the translation apparatus in eukaryotes is a complex system with a number of specific features, which are different from those in prokaryotes.
